purpose: Structured California recovery ledger linking continued FEMA housing support, residual-need recontact, and CalAssist mortgage relief while preserving household receipt, rebuild completion, and durable housing as open.

events.date_precision: State update published in June 2026; assistance total reported as of June 12, 2026
events.denominator: More than 35,000 households reported assisted and more than $177 million awarded; aggregate program denominator, not a named-household longitudinal panel
events.method: Structured extraction from California official recovery update and related official continued-assistance notice
events.missingness: No household-level payment, award date, amount adequacy, rental end, repair completion, permanent housing, work, health, debt, or later stability
events.exposure: FEMA housing support was extended through July 2027 while survivors rebuild; households with exhausted insurance living expenses or remaining unmet needs were directed to re-contact FEMA
events.alternatives_before_action: Insurance, local or nonprofit aid, household resources, rental or hotel options, and other housing or repair channels may have been available; household channel switching and non-use are not observed
events.immediate_burden_or_benefit: The extension preserves a longer assistance window and makes residual housing need administratively actionable, but does not establish usable recovery for any named household
events.choice_or_response: Survivors may re-contact FEMA for continued rental or repair assistance; individual recontact, acceptance, non-use, and appeal are not observed
events.person_or_actor_with_control: FEMA and California control program rules, extension timing, eligibility communication, and delivery routes; survivors navigate those constraints
events.remedy_or_institutional_response: FEMA continued housing support through July 2027 and California reported aggregate households assisted and dollars awarded
events.remedy_receipt: Aggregate assistance is reported; household-level issuance, receipt, adequacy, and housing result are unverified
events.durability_followup: No linked follow-up shows rental exit, repair completion, permanent housing, repeat need, or durable stability
events.immediate_outcome: The recovery route advances from one-time eligibility and payment visibility to a continuing housing-support clock and a residual-need recontact route
events.protected_outcome: Some households may have received continued housing or repair support; protected housing and agency are not established
events.sacrificed_outcome: Remaining rent, repair, debt, displacement, and navigation burdens cannot be assigned to households from the aggregate record
events.cost_risk_transfer: Long recovery and recontact requirements may transfer timing, documentation, and residual-loss risk to survivors, but distribution is not measured
events.later_outcome: Stable housing, return, work and health recovery, trust, complaint, political action, and exit remain open
events.meaning_and_attribution: No household-level fairness, blame, legitimacy, or trust change is observed
events.public_or_collective_response: State and federal administration is observed; survivor organizing and political response are not
events.counterexample: An extension can help a household recover, while another household may fail to recontact, remain in temporary housing, or receive inadequate support
events.source_and_uncertainty: California official recovery update and continued-assistance notice; aggregate program reporting does not establish a household panel

events.geography: California; Los Angeles wildfire long-term housing recovery
events.date_precision: July 2026 bulletin; exact household payment dates are not reported
events.denominator: More than 1,100 homeowners reported assisted; program maximums are up to 12 months of mortgage payments and up to $100,000, not an average award
events.method: Structured extraction from California official Long-Term Housing Recovery bulletin
events.missingness: No named homeowner, lender decision, insurance release, payment receipt, mortgage balance, rebuild completion, return, or durable housing outcome
events.exposure: CalAssist provided a mortgage-payment bridge while insurance and rebuilding processes continued; California also urged lenders to release insurance proceeds promptly
events.alternatives_before_action: Insurance proceeds, lender forbearance, savings, family resources, rental housing, or other aid may have been alternatives; selection and feasibility are not observed
events.immediate_burden_or_benefit: Mortgage relief can preserve housing finance during rebuilding, while delayed insurance release can slow reconstruction; household-level net effect is not observed
events.choice_or_response: Homeowners, insurers, and lenders had to navigate payment and release processes; applications, denials, appeals, and switching are not retained
events.person_or_actor_with_control: California, CalAssist, lenders, and insurers control different parts of the bridge; homeowners bear the consequences of timing and documentation
events.remedy_or_institutional_response: CalAssist reported mortgage assistance and the state publicly pressed lenders to release insurance proceeds promptly
events.remedy_receipt: Aggregate homeowner assistance is reported; named payment receipt, sufficiency, and rebuilding result are unverified
events.durability_followup: No linked record shows whether mortgage relief ended in completed repair, return, debt sustainability, or stable housing
events.immediate_outcome: The recovery map gains a financial-control stage: housing recovery depends on both public assistance and the timing of insurance and mortgage funds
events.protected_outcome: Some homeowners may have avoided immediate mortgage loss or gained time to rebuild; durable housing is not established
events.sacrificed_outcome: Payment delay, coverage gaps, debt, displacement, and repair delay remain unmeasured at household level
events.cost_risk_transfer: Insurance and lender timing can transfer reconstruction and debt risk to homeowners, but the affected distribution is not measured
events.later_outcome: Rebuild completion, return, work and health recovery, trust, complaint, political action, and exit remain open
events.meaning_and_attribution: No homeowner-level fairness, blame, legitimacy, or trust change is observed
events.public_or_collective_response: Official coordination and public pressure on lenders are observed; homeowner organizing and political response are not
events.counterexample: Mortgage assistance can protect a homeowner while insurance delay still prevents repair, or a homeowner can rebuild without using CalAssist
events.source_and_uncertainty: California official bulletin; reported recipients and program maximums are not a payment or rebuild-completion panel

arrows.to: ongoing rental or repair assistance route
arrows.evidence: California reported FEMA support extended through July 2027 and a recontact route for survivors with exhausted insurance living expenses or unmet needs
arrows.counterexample: An available route does not establish that a household recontacted, qualified, received, or found the support adequate
arrows.remaining_gap: Named household recontact, decision, issuance, receipt, amount adequacy, and housing result

arrows.evidence: The official record reports more than 35,000 households assisted and more than $177 million awarded, but no household recovery panel
arrows.counterexample: Aggregate assistance can coexist with completed recovery for some households and prolonged temporary housing for others
arrows.remaining_gap: Household payment, rental exit, repair completion, permanent housing, and later stability

arrows.to: time to rebuild and avoid immediate mortgage loss
arrows.evidence: California reported more than 1,100 homeowners assisted with up to 12 months of mortgage payments and up to $100,000
arrows.counterexample: Program maximums and aggregate recipient counts do not show a named homeowner's payment, timing, or avoided loss
arrows.remaining_gap: Named application, award, payment receipt, lender status, and counterfactual housing or debt outcome

arrows.evidence: The bulletin links prompt release of insurance proceeds to the ability to rebuild and records state pressure on lenders
arrows.counterexample: A homeowner may rebuild without CalAssist, or receive mortgage relief while insurance or construction delays continue
arrows.remaining_gap: Insurer decision and payment, lender action, construction milestone, return, debt adequacy, and durable housing

arrows.to: trust, repeat need, or political response
arrows.evidence: Official records document continued assistance and unresolved financial or housing processes, but do not follow household meaning or action
arrows.counterexample: Continued aid may increase trust for one household and frustration or exit for another
arrows.remaining_gap: Repeated contact, unmet need, trust, complaint, organizing, voting, switching, or exit

boundary: This ledger formalizes a longer disaster-recovery clock and a mortgage/insurance bridge. It does not estimate household receipt, adequacy, rebuild completion, stable housing, trust, or political action.
storage_boundary: Only official aggregate and program-level claims are retained; no survivor identifiers, payment file, insurer file, lender file, or personally identifying information is included.
